I'm Benjamin Telkamp — a statistics teacher and researcher, and for more than twenty-five years I have been helping people who decided somewhere along the way that statistics was "not for them". Under the name WISI (*Wiskunde &amp; Statistiek Inzichtelijk*, Mathematics &amp; Statistics Made Clear) I work with the school pupil who has lost the thread, the student whose exam is coming closer far too fast, and the PhD candidate with a mountain of data and a deadline.

<!-- MIEKE: "formules opdreunen" — gekozen "reciting formulas"; alternatief "rattling off
     formulas" (spreektaliger). "een trucje dat het tentamen nét overleeft" — gekozen "a trick
     that only just survives the exam". -->
My job is not reciting formulas. It is explaining hard material in such a way that real insight forms — and not just a trick that only just survives the exam.

<!-- BEN: "Meer over waar ik vandaan kom" linkt naar cv-en, de bestaande Engelse cv. -->
Everything on this site is free for anyone who learns from it on their own, and it will stay that way — clarity is something I would rather give away. But sometimes you need more than a book: someone who sits down beside you, looks over your shoulder, and makes it clear together with you. That is what you can hire. The books are free; my time isn't. More about where I come from and what I have done is in my [CV](../cv-en.html).

## Tutoring in maths &amp; statistics

<!-- MIEKE: "begrip dat klopt" — gekozen "understanding that adds up"; alternatief
     "understanding that holds". -->
<!-- BEN: "in English or in Dutch" staat niet in het Nederlands. Ik zette het erbij omdat je
     les geeft aan Webster University (Engelstalig, staat in cv-en). Klopt het niet, dan eruit. -->
One-to-one, at your pace, in English or in Dutch. I look for the short route and the picture that sticks — not dry rules, but understanding that adds up. That works especially well if you tend to drop out at dense text and long routes; I know that from myself, and I build on it. From secondary school to university, with SPSS, R or JASP.

## Crash courses &amp; exam training

Exam in sight and the material still not in? In a few focused sessions we go from panic to overview: what you really need to be able to do, which test belongs to which question, and how to work it out without losing yourself along the way.

## Thesis supervision

<!-- MIEKE: "scriptie of thesis" — in Nederland twee woorden voor bachelor en master; in het
     Britse Engels is "dissertation" vaak het woord daarvoor, in het Amerikaanse juist voor de
     promotie. Gekozen: "thesis or dissertation". -->
Stuck in your thesis or dissertation? I walk with you from research question to analysis to writing it up: choosing the right method, getting your data through the statistics (SPSS, R or JASP), and getting your results onto the page, neatly and by the APA rules.

## Research supervision

<!-- MIEKE: "reviewers vóór zijn" — gekozen "getting there before the reviewers do", de vorm
     die solomon-en ook gebruikt ("you get there before the sceptic does"). -->
<!-- BEN: "GGZ Delfland" kreeg een uitleg tussen haakjes, voor wie de naam niet kent. -->
For PhD candidates and researchers I think along from analysis plan to article: choosing models and running them in R, making the case for methodological choices, getting tables and figures ready for APA, and getting there before the reviewers do. From raw data to a manuscript that stands — the work a data scientist does, but done so that you yourself understand what is happening, and can defend it. I have done this for PhD candidates at GGZ Delfland (a Dutch mental-health provider), among others.

## AI, but with understanding

A language model will give you a quick answer to your statistics question — just not always the right one. I help you judge the output, take the mistakes out and understand what it actually says, so that you use AI as a tool and not as a black box you simply have to trust.

## Guest lectures &amp; workshops

<!-- MIEKE: "dezelfde didactiek als de werkboeken hier" — gekozen "the same way of teaching as
     the books on this site", want "didactics" is in het Engels een zeldzaam en Latijns woord. -->
For degree programmes, universities of applied sciences and teams, I teach statistics that sticks: a guest lecture, a workshop or a series made to measure, with the same way of teaching as the books on this site.

<!-- MIEKE: "niet alleen over de sommen" — gekozen "not only about the sums" (Brits: sommen =
     rekenwerk). Een Amerikaanse lezer kan "sums" als totalen lezen; alternatief "the maths". -->
And sometimes it isn't only about the sums. With the students I supervise, the conversation regularly turns to the life around it as well — getting stuck, making choices, what you are actually doing it for. If there is a need for that, I am glad to make room for it.

## Rates

<!-- MIEKE: "helderheid mag niet op geld stuklopen" — gekozen "clarity shouldn't run aground on
     money" (stuklopen = vastlopen als een schip); alternatief "clarity shouldn't fail for want
     of money". -->
I don't have a fixed price list: what it costs depends on what is needed, and that differs rather a lot between a single tutoring session and walking alongside a whole research project. Just ask, and I'll make you a proposal to fit. And if money is tight? Say so — then we'll see together what is possible. Clarity shouldn't run aground on money.
